thread:
maia: Heads-up — I'm seeing inconsistent apples-to-apples numbers between two runs of the same model. Suspect kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache warmup differences. Can we lock down a harness checklist?

samir: yes. minimal checklist I want: same prompt set, same tokenizer binary/version, identical decoding params (temp/top_p/beam/stop), same max_new_tokens, same seed for sampling, same padding strategy, and identical batch-shape distribution. Replay traces over synthetic where possible.

taylor: fwiw we recently changed dynamic batching to group by arrival time window not seq len; that introduced extra padding and accounted for ~12% p95 regression in last perf run. see quick note: https://ci.example/reports/1764 (flamegraphs attached).

perf-bot: Profile uploaded: https://perf.example/reports/1765004321/flame.html — top hotspots: kernel_launch_overhead, memcpy_h2d, kv_cache_miss_handler.

lee: KV cache behavior is huge. Cold-start from empty KV for every replayed req skews tail. Proposal: prime KV cache in harness by sending deterministic prefixes before measuring. Example warmup call: `./replay_harness.py --model rdx-xlarge --seed 42 --prime-prefixes warmup_prompts.txt --replay-rate 200`

jia: also callout tokenizer alignment — must use the exact same tokenizer commit and `tokenizer.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)` when constructing inputs for both models. Mismatched tokenization will change token counts and padding. Double-check stop-sequence matching by token ids.

alex: on synthetic traffic: Poisson arrivals produce different batching behavior than our prod traces. For apples-to-apples we should replay a sampled production trace (arrival timestamps + concurrency) and also run a controlled Poisson run to isolate batching effects. sample config (harness):
```
replay: true
trace_file: traces/2026-03-12-prod.json
concurrency_cap: 64
max_batch_size: 32
decode: { temperature: 0.0, top_p: 0.95, max_new_tokens: 128 }
```

morgan: Action items I can take: 1) add tokenizer pin + checksum to harness, 2) add KV warmup step, 3) pin kernel selector logging (environment var REDWOOD_KERNEL_TRACE=1), 4) run 3 seeds and compare median/p95 and include per-kernel breakdown. I'll kickoff runs today. :rocket:

maia: SG. also let's ensure we pin CUDA/cuDNN and quantization profile (fp16 vs int8) in the run metadata so apples-to-apples includes hardware/quant settings.

samir: tiny nit — when reporting, include exact decode bits: `stop_sequences` as token ids and the tokenizer version. makes regressions reproducible.

taylor: after warmup + pinned tokenizer I expect the p95 gap to shrink. if not, next step is to force kernel selection to the old policy and rerun to isolate kernel selector impact.

lee: perf-bot also flagged a few stable regressions across models when `batching.window_ms` was increased from 8 -> 20. worth rolling back for an A/B to confirm.

morgan: noted, I'll add an A/B to the harness (window_ms=8 vs 20) and include per-batch padding waste metric.

maia: perfect. let's keep the thread here for results. when you have the first run link drop it in the thread. :eyes:
